name: AIProtect
description: Checks links before you open them, and warns you before you share personal information with an AI assistant.
//permissions: Deliberately minimal, and each one is here for a named reason. Every
permission is something a reviewer -- and a customer -- has to be told
about, and this extension can see what someone is about to type into a
chatbot. The B2B extension it was forked from asks for eleven
declarativeNetRequest. None of those are needed to warn somebody.
storage      the device credential and the person's settings
tabs         to show a warning page in the tab that triggered it
webNavigation  to check a link BEFORE the page loads
notifications  to tell someone what was blocked while they were away
//host_permissions: http://*/* is NOT requested. Safe Links works from the webNavigation
URL alone -- the extension never needs to read the contents of an
arbitrary page. The content script is restricted to the handful of AI
assistants where Privacy Guard actually does something, so on every
other site on the web this extension cannot read anything at all.
